Resolve site, patch, and year indices for FINN inputs

Source: R/createInputs.R
resolveSiteIDs.Rd

Joins tree, environment, and observation tables; assigns integer indices for site, patch and year; standardizes species coding; and returns aligned data plus optional initial cohorts.

Usage

resolveSiteIDs(
  tree_dt,
  env_dt,
  obs_dt,
  createInitCohorts = TRUE,
  time_axis = c("annual", "census")
)

Arguments

tree_dt

data.table with tree-level data including siteName, patchName, year, species_name, dbh, status, living, and optional trees.

env_dt

data.table with environment data including siteName and year (calendar year; see Details for the years needed).

obs_dt

data.table with observations including siteName, patchName, year, species_name, and stand metrics (ba, dbh, trees, growth, mort, n_at_risk, n_died, reg, period_length), as returned by makeObsData.

createInitCohorts

logical. If TRUE, build FINN initial cohorts from the living trees of the first inventory (year == 0) on either time axis. Default TRUE.

time_axis

"annual" (default) or "census". "census" is the axis of FINN 0.1.0: year is the index of the inventory (0, 1, 2, ...), one simulation step is one census interval (period_length = 1), env_dt keeps the inventory years, and the observations of the first inventory stay in obs_dt. Use it with makeObsData(rates = "interval"). Unlike 0.1.0, which built the initial cohorts from the second inventory, the census axis now starts from the first one, so 0.1.0 results are not reproduced exactly.

Value

A list with:

  • siteID_dt: site/patch/year index map (OrigYear is the calendar year).

  • tree_dt: tree table with indices and standardized species.

  • env_dt: environment table with indices, the years of the simulation: siteID, year and the predictors, what fit(env = ) takes (siteID_dt maps the ids back to the site names).

  • obs_dt: site-aggregated observations by species, with period_length.

  • obs_dt_patches: patch-level observations by species.

  • species_dt: species lookup (species, species_name).

  • initCohorts (optional): FINN CohortMat object.

  • initCohort_dt (optional): trees used to build cohorts.

The list can be stored with saveRDS() and read back with readRDS(): initCohorts keeps a plain R copy of its arrays and rebuilds its torch tensors, which saveRDS() cannot store, when fit(), simulateForest() or predict.finn_class() use it (or by x$initCohorts$restore(), see CohortMat). Cohorts saved with FINN before 0.2.0 carry no such copy; rebuild them from the table with x$initCohorts <- makeInitCohorts(x$initCohort_dt, Nspecies = nrow(x$species_dt)).

Details

With time_axis = "annual" (the default) one simulation step is one year: year becomes the number of years since the first inventory of the site's patch (0 at the first inventory, e.g. 10 and 20 at the next two), the first inventory is the initial state (the initial cohorts, not an observation), the observations carry period_length in years, and env_dt is returned with one row per site and year 1..Tmax, Tmax being the longest time from a first to a last inventory. The environment row of year \(k\) drives the simulated year that ends at year \(k\), so an inventory \(k\) years after the first is compared with the stand after \(k\) simulated years. env_dt therefore needs one row per site and calendar year from the year after the site's first inventory to Tmax years after it; a climate that does not change is repeated for every year.

See also

makeObsData for the step before, makeInitCohorts for the initial cohorts on their own, fit and finn_data for where the tables go

Examples

library(data.table)
# eight Oregon FIA plots, three inventories each; see the data-preparation vignette
tree_dt <- fread(system.file("extdata", "example_tree_dt.csv", package = "FINN"))
env_dt  <- fread(system.file("extdata", "example_env_dt.csv",  package = "FINN"))
obs <- makeObsData(tree_dt[complete == TRUE], plotsize = 0.06, aggregate_by_site = FALSE,
                   fix_period_length = 10, NspeciesQuantile = 0.98)
#> excluded 0 sites due to period length not beeing 10
#> excluded 0 sites due to dbh_growth being not within the range of -10 and 50
#> Nspecies set to 11 to cover 98% of individuals
#> Selected species: Pseudotsuga menziesii, Pinus ponderosa, Tsuga mertensiana, Pinus contorta, Abies grandis, Pinus monticola, Abies concolor, Abies shastensis, other, Juniperus occidentalis, Larix occidentalis
#> Combined 4 unselected species into 'other'
#> actuall number of species including 'others' is 12
#> Filtered to sites with at least 2 years and all patches having the same number of years:
#> Sites with 3 Inventories: 1056
#> Sites have between 4 and 4 patches
#> Kept obs_dt unaggregated by siteName. For aggregated data, set aggregate_by_site = TRUE

# Names become integer ids shared by every table, calendar years become years
# since the first inventory: 0 (the initial state), 10 and 20. Pass the tree
# list makeObsData() returned: it carries the same species lumping as obs_dt.
# createInitCohorts = FALSE leaves out the starting cohorts, which need torch.
inputs <- resolveSiteIDs(tree_dt = obs$tree_dt, obs_dt = obs$obs_dt, env_dt = env_dt,
                         createInitCohorts = FALSE)
inputs$species_dt
#>     species           species_name
#>       <int>                 <char>
#>  1:       9  Pseudotsuga menziesii
#>  2:      11                  other
#>  3:       8        Pinus ponderosa
#>  4:       5     Larix occidentalis
#>  5:       2          Abies grandis
#>  6:       4 Juniperus occidentalis
#>  7:       7        Pinus monticola
#>  8:       6         Pinus contorta
#>  9:       1         Abies concolor
#> 10:      10      Tsuga mertensiana
#> 11:       3       Abies shastensis
head(inputs$obs_dt)      # per site, year and species: what fit(data = ) takes
#>    siteID  year    ba   dbh trees growth growth_n  mort n_at_risk n_died   reg
#>     <int> <int> <num> <num> <num>  <num>    <int> <num>     <int>  <int> <num>
#> 1:      1    10     0   NaN     0    NaN        0    NA         0      0     0
#> 2:      1    20     0   NaN     0    NaN        0    NA         0      0     0
#> 3:      2    10     0   NaN     0    NaN        0    NA         0      0     0
#> 4:      2    20     0   NaN     0    NaN        0    NA         0      0     0
#> 5:      3    10     0   NaN     0    NaN        0    NA         0      0     0
#> 6:      3    20     0   NaN     0    NaN        0    NA         0      0     0
#>    species   species_name period_length
#>      <int>         <char>         <int>
#> 1:       1 Abies concolor            10
#> 2:       1 Abies concolor            10
#> 3:       1 Abies concolor            10
#> 4:       1 Abies concolor            10
#> 5:       1 Abies concolor            10
#> 6:       1 Abies concolor            10
range(inputs$env_dt$year) # one row per site and simulated year: what fit(env = ) takes
#> [1]  1 20
head(inputs$siteID_dt)   # the map back to the inventory's own names
#>    siteID patchID siteName  patchName  year OrigYear
#>     <int>   <int>   <char>     <char> <int>    <int>
#> 1:      1       1 11_66410 11_66410_1     0     2001
#> 2:      1       2 11_66410 11_66410_2     0     2001
#> 3:      1       3 11_66410 11_66410_3     0     2001
#> 4:      1       4 11_66410 11_66410_4     0     2001
#> 5:      1       1 11_66410 11_66410_1    10     2011
#> 6:      1       2 11_66410 11_66410_2    10     2011
# with torch, the same call also builds the starting cohorts (a CohortMat)
inputs <- resolveSiteIDs(tree_dt = obs$tree_dt, obs_dt = obs$obs_dt, env_dt = env_dt)
inputs$initCohorts$dims  # sites, patches, cohorts
#> [1]  8  4 15
